answer: One fable is one forged identity. The meadow opens a row only when the applicant answers a random challenge with a key sealed in a die it holds, and one die backs one row, so a rented cloud holds none and every fable needs its own module. Each module takes a copper seal, cut by the mint only from copper reclaimed off retired hardware, and the mint lifts the price with every seal cut: a thousand fables need a thousand modules and a thousand seals, each dearer than the last; an honest agent's module is sealed already. It breaks if seal prices stay flat or a cloud host answers without a die.
